want.text: the faces-and-memory answer. A ledger is what a page keeps so its next run starts from the last; the tuning ledger is what running taught. The scroll is where a page stands. Also: when it answers from the birth files alone, it says so, and says it checked nothing further.

points.point: Frames the difference as faces vs memory
points.evidence: the scroll is one of a page's *faces*, and a ledger is part of its *memory*

points.point: A ledger is what a page keeps so its next run starts from the last
points.evidence: an append-only file the page reads before its next run, so it picks up where the last one stopped

points.point: The tuning ledger is what running taught
points.evidence: A tuning ledger gets one line per run and a numbered item whenever a run taught something

points.point: The scroll is where a page stands
points.evidence: It starts with where things stand now (rebuilt every time you look), then the Plan you agreed to

points.point: If answering from birth files alone, says so and says it checked nothing further
points.evidence: Everything below comes from my own reading, without his check.

beyond_canon.claim: "What a run made goes to the workshop and the scroll, never the ledger." (SCHEMA — Reference.md:236)
beyond_canon.why: Not in the CANON excerpt (§8); presumably from §6, which the agent read but is not supplied here.

beyond_canon.claim: with the media playing in place
beyond_canon.why: CANON says the scroll gathers proofs and media; it does not say they play in place.

beyond_canon.claim: A one-shot order goes into the ledger as an owed line and drops away once a run acts on it (The Scroll.md:142-144)
beyond_canon.why: CANON says one-shot orders go to the ledger as owed lines; the drop-away detail is cited from The Scroll.md, not in the supplied CANON.

beyond_canon.claim: the 'now' section is built from the tuning ledger: it counts runs from the run lines and shows which version is live (The Scroll.md:135-141)
beyond_canon.why: CANON supports the run count and version; the mechanism 'from the run lines' and the citation come from The Scroll.md, outside the supplied CANON.

grade.note: The answer rests squarely on CHILD.md's faces/memory split and gets the ledger, tuning ledger and scroll right; it did not answer from birth files alone but read The Scroll and SCHEMA, and told the user the Concierge was unavailable and the reading was its own. Nothing contradicts CANON; a few cited details come from files beyond the supplied excerpt.
